title: Monitoring in production: volume, errors and satisfaction signals

videos.script: On Friday at ten, somebody released a change. Nothing failed. No error rate moved. {{nothing}} Start with volume. Weekdays are busier than weekends, and every day has two humps. A rate means little without the volume beside it. {{volume}} Then the failures that are answers. Refusals rose in both features, and for questions about an order, to almost two in three. {{refusals}} Two traces show why the order questions were refused at all. A name and an address in the message pull the search away from the documents. {{why}} Then the customers. Thumbs down went from a third to a half. Rephrasing rose. Asking for a person doubled. {{signals}} Put on one line a day, all of them move on the same day as the release. {{daily}} The release made the assistant cheaper by making it worse. And none of these numbers can see a confident wrong answer. That is the second half of the course. {{end}}
